newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suspected Corsican guerrillas bomb public office.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Corsican guerrillas bomb public office.

text.p: Suspected Corsican guerrillas bombed a public works office on the French Mediterranean island on Wednesday in the first attack of the New Year, police said.
The blast virtually destroyed the local government public works office in Ventiseri-Pont du Travo in southeastern Corsica. Police said the wrecked building would have to be demolished.

No one was hurt in the bombing and no one immediately claimed responsibility for the blast at five minutes after midnight (2305 GMT), apparently timed to stress that guerrillas plan no truce for 1997.
Corsican separatists have recently stepped up their 20-year-campaign for greater autonomy from mainland France during which they have planted thousands of bombs, mostly at night to avoid casualties.
In a separate attack apparently unrelated to the guerrillas, a young couple were shot dead at their home shortly after midnight in the southern mountain village of Aullene.
Police were holding a 28-year-old man suspected of shooting the woman and man, both aged 25. Investigators said the motive for the crime was unknown but did not seem political.

Corsica has been seeking to shake off a reputation for lawlessness -- murder rates are far higher than on the mainland. In 1996, there were 22 killings on the island of 250,000 people, down from 40 in 1995.
